problem: Grid-scale energy generation requires dispatchable, zero-emission power sources with high conversion efficiency.
unexploited_phenomenon: Self-sustainable thermophotovoltaic systems designed as standalone power generation assets
intervention: Implementation of thermophotovoltaic systems using thermal energy storage to generate electricity independently from the grid
governing_variables: Temperature of thermal storage (K), bandgap of photovoltaic material (eV), spectral efficiency (%)
predicted_effect: 15-25% improvement in conversion efficiency compared to conventional thermal-to-electric conversion
equations: η = 1 - (T_c/T_h) (Carnot efficiency limit), η_TPV = η_thermal × η_photon × η_electrical (thermophotovoltaic efficiency)
boundary_conditions: Requires high-temperature thermal storage (>1000K), sensitive to spectral matching between thermal emitter and PV cell, efficiency decreases with temperature differential
cross_domain_transition: Space power systems -> terrestrial grid-scale generation + Enables dispatchable zero-emission power with high conversion efficiency

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Conventional thermal power plants with conversion limited by Carnot efficiency
baseline.baseline_metric: 30-40% conversion efficiency for conventional thermal plants
baseline.candidate_metric: 45-65% conversion efficiency through thermophotovoltaic conversion

killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Spectral matching efficiency between thermal emitter and PV cell at operational temperatures
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Measured efficiency falls below 35% at optimal operating temperature

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Energy storage systems need to combine high efficiency with space flexibility for grid-scale applications.
unexploited_phenomenon: Hydro-pneumatic energy storage using pump turbines to displace a virtual liquid piston for air compression
intervention: Development of a hydro-pneumatic energy storage system using rotodynamic multi-stage pump-turbines
governing_variables: Pump-turbine efficiency (%), compression ratio (dimensionless), heat transfer coefficient (W/m²K)
predicted_effect: 10-20% improvement in round-trip efficiency compared to pure pneumatic storage
equations: η_roundtrip = η_pump × η_turbine × η_compression (round-trip efficiency), ΔU = m·Cv·ΔT (internal energy change)
boundary_conditions: Effective for medium-duration storage (hours), requires efficient heat management during compression/expansion, limited by mechanical losses in pump-turbine
cross_domain_transition: Hydraulic systems -> grid-scale energy storage + Combines high efficiency of hydraulic systems with flexibility of pneumatic storage

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Pure pneumatic energy storage systems with lower efficiency due to heat losses
baseline.baseline_metric: 40-50% round-trip efficiency for conventional compressed air storage
baseline.candidate_metric: 50-70% round-trip efficiency through hydraulic-pneumatic hybrid approach

killer_experiment.experiment: LAB-scale hydro-pneumatic test rig with pump-turbine, pressure vessel, and efficiency measurement equipment
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Round-trip efficiency of the hybrid hydraulic-pneumatic system
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Measured round-trip efficiency falls below 45%

problem: Marine current turbines generate fluctuating power due to tidal periodicity and swell effects, requiring efficient energy storage for grid stability.
unexploited_phenomenon: Energy storage systems specifically designed for smoothing power fluctuations in marine current turbines
intervention: Integration of energy storage systems with marine current turbines to smooth power fluctuations
governing_variables: Turbine power output (W), storage capacity (Wh), response time (s), conversion efficiency (%)
predicted_effect: 30-50% reduction in power fluctuation amplitude compared to direct grid connection
equations: P_smooth = P_raw - ΔP_storage (smoothed power output), η_storage = E_out/E_in (storage efficiency)
boundary_conditions: Effective for tidal fluctuation periods (hours), requires high cycle-life storage, limited by round-trip efficiency of storage systems
cross_domain_transition: Wave energy systems -> marine current generation + Enables stable power output from inherently variable marine resources

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Direct grid connection of marine current turbines with fluctuating power output
baseline.baseline_metric: High power fluctuation (up to 100% of rated output) due to tidal variations
baseline.candidate_metric: 30-50% reduction in power fluctuation through energy storage integration

killer_experiment.experiment: BENCH-scale simulation of marine current turbine output with and without energy storage, power fluctuation analysis
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Round-trip efficiency of energy storage integration with marine turbines
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Storage round-trip efficiency falls below 60%

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

verified_bindings.span: The performance and economic viability of utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) plants are critically influenced by location-specific climatic factors, yet conventional site selection often overlooks thermodynamic quality and long-term degradation.

This study presents the design, simulation and performance analysis of a 650 kW on-grid solar electricity generation system for a rural community in Rivers State, Nigeria, using the photovoltaic system (PVsyst) software.

This paper presents a novel Chaotic Lévy flight-enhanced Grey wolf optimizer (CLF-GWO) algorithm for multi-objective optimization of grid-connected solar photovoltaic power plants, validated using 36-month meteorological data from Guwahati, Assam.
The proposed algorithm integrates logistic chaotic maps for population diversity, tent chaotic maps for adaptive parameter control, and Lévy flight mechanisms for improved escape from local optima.

Applied to six climatic zones in Saudi Arabia for a standardized 100 MW plant, the analysis reveals that the highest energy-yield location (Riyadh, 224.7 GWh/year) does not achieve the highest exergy efficiency (Abha, 16.1%)

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

problem: Bearing wear in wind turbine drivetrains leads to costly replacements and downtime.
causal_chain: reduced peak stresses on bearing components
unexploited_phenomenon: Strategic pre-misalignment to redistribute loads and reduce stress concentrations in bearing components
intervention: Drivetrain system with engineered pre-misalignment during installation
governing_variables: Misalignment angle (degrees), load distribution factor, stress concentration (MPa)
predicted_effect: 25-40% increase in bearing lifespan by reducing peak stresses by 15-25%
equations: σ_max = K_t * σ_nominal - maximum stress with stress concentration factor
F_d = F * cos(θ) - load distribution as function of misalignment
boundary_conditions: Effective for specific bearing types and load conditions; requires precise installation; optimal angle varies by application
cross_domain_transition: Industrial machinery bearing design -> wind energy, applying pre-misalignment techniques to reduce bearing wear

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Perfectly aligned bearing systems
baseline.baseline_metric: Average bearing replacement interval of 7-10 years
baseline.candidate_metric: Extended bearing replacement interval of 9-14 years

killer_experiment.experiment: Accelerated bearing life test rig with controlled misalignment, comparing wear rates between perfectly aligned and pre-misaligned bearings
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: The optimal pre-misalignment angle for different bearing sizes and load conditions
killer_experiment.kill_condition: No improvement in bearing lifespan or increased wear with pre-misalignment

unexploited_phenomenon: Electrical signature analysis as a non-intrusive method to detect mechanical degradation through electrical system monitoring
intervention: Continuous electrical signature monitoring system with anomaly detection algorithms
governing_variables: Harmonic distortion (%), current imbalance (A), voltage fluctuations (V)
predicted_effect: 50-70% earlier detection of material degradation compared to traditional methods, reducing maintenance costs by 20-35%
equations: THD = √(Σ(I_n²)/I_1²) - total harmonic distortion
I_imbalance = |I_max - I_min|/I_avg - current imbalance factor

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

verified_bindings.span: As part of the drive train and generator track this paper will present the results of a comparative study on the availability of offshore wind turbine drive train types. Twelve different drive train types will be compared.

This paper investigates geared and direct-drive permanent magnet generators for a typical offshore wind turbine, providing a detailed comparison of various wind turbine drivetrain configurations in order to minimise the Cost of Energy.

As part of the drive train and generator track this paper will present the results of a comparative study on the availability of offshore wind turbine drive train types. Twelve different drive train types will be compared.

The permanent magnet generator topologies considered include a direct-drive machine and single stage, two-stage or three-stage gearbox driven generators. The cost of energy calculations are based on initial capital costs, the costs of manufacture, installation, operations and maintenance, with particular focus on improved calculations of the annual energy yield with better availability estimations and gearbox loss modelling

There is currently a lack of offshore availability data for wind turbines with different drive trains. This paper provides a unique overview of expected availability of various offshore drive trains. These results could contribute to future studies or models of offshore annual production, cost of energy and so on

problem: Inability to measure critical drivetrain parameters in offshore wind turbines due to sensing blind spots, leading to undetected mechanical failures.
unexploited_phenomenon: Modal parameter tracking of offshore wind turbine drivetrain systems
intervention: Automatic tracking system that continuously monitors modal parameters to detect early signs of drivetrain degradation
governing_variables: Natural frequency (Hz), damping ratio, mode shape amplitude
predicted_effect: 40-70% reduction in undetected drivetrain failures by detecting modal parameter shifts indicative of developing faults
equations: f_n = (1/2π)√(k/m) where f_n is natural frequency (Hz), k is stiffness (N/m), m is mass (kg)
boundary_conditions: Effective in operational conditions with sufficient excitation; fails during low wind periods or with insufficient vibration sources
cross_domain_transition: Aerospace structural health monitoring -> wind energy, transferring modal analysis techniques to detect mechanical degradation in rotating machinery

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Traditional vibration monitoring with fixed sensors
baseline.baseline_metric: Limited to detecting faults after significant damage has occurred
baseline.candidate_metric: Early detection of developing faults through continuous modal parameter tracking

killer_experiment.experiment: Laboratory drivetrain test rig with controlled excitation, comparing modal tracking system against traditional vibration sensors
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether modal parameter changes can be reliably correlated with specific fault types
killer_experiment.kill_condition: No statistically significant correlation between modal parameter changes and fault development

problem: Inability to detect early-stage bearing defects in wind turbine drivetrains due to mechanical sensing limitations.
unexploited_phenomenon: Electrical signature analysis for detecting drivetrain bearing defects
intervention: Non-invasive monitoring system that analyzes electrical signatures to detect bearing defects without direct mechanical access
governing_variables: Harmonic distortion components, sideband frequencies, amplitude modulation
predicted_effect: 50-80% reduction in undetected bearing failures by detecting electrical signatures indicative of developing defects
equations: THD = √(ΣV_n²)/V_1 × 100% where THD is total harmonic distortion, V_n is harmonic voltage component, V_1 is fundamental voltage
boundary_conditions: Effective with sufficient electrical load; may have reduced sensitivity during low power operation
cross_domain_transition: Motor fault detection -> wind turbine drivetrains, transferring electrical signature analysis techniques to detect mechanical faults

baseline.baseline_metric: Limited accessibility in offshore environments, especially for internal components
baseline.candidate_metric: Early detection of bearing defects through electrical signature analysis

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

governing_variables: Misalignment angle (θ, radians), load distribution factor (LDF), contact stress (σ, Pa), bearing life (L, hours)

A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

verified_bindings.span: As part of the drive train and generator track this paper will present the results of a comparative study on the availability of offshore wind turbine drive train types. Twelve different drive train types will be compared.

This paper investigates geared and direct-drive permanent magnet generators for a typical offshore wind turbine, providing a detailed comparison of various wind turbine drivetrain configurations in order to minimise the Cost of Energy.
The permanent magnet generator topologies considered include a direct-drive machine and single stage, two-stage or three-stage gearbox driven generators.

problem: Wind turbine drivetrain bearings fail prematurely due to misalignment-induced stress concentrations.
unexploited_phenomenon: The beneficial effect of controlled pre-misalignment on bearing reliability as documented in wind turbine applications.
intervention: Implement controlled pre-misalignment in industrial machinery bearing systems during installation.
governing_variables: Misalignment angle (θ, degrees), contact stress distribution (σ, MPa), bearing load capacity (F, N)
predicted_effect: 30-50% reduction in bearing failure rate in industrial machinery due to more uniform stress distribution.
equations: σ = F/(A·cos(θ)), where A is contact area
Life ∝ (σ/σ₀)^(-3.33) (Lundberg-Palmgren equation)
boundary_conditions: Effective for moderate misalignment angles (0.1-0.5°); fails under excessive misalignment (>1°) or shock loads
cross_domain_transition: Wind power generation -> industrial machinery, transferring the pre-misalignment technique to extend bearing life in other rotating equipment

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Undetected drivetrain failures in manufacturing equipment lead to unexpected downtime and production losses.
unexploited_phenomenon: Electrical signature analysis for detecting drivetrain faults without direct mechanical access.
intervention: Deploy electrical signature analysis systems on manufacturing equipment motors to detect developing mechanical faults.
governing_variables: Current harmonics (I_h, A), fault frequency (f_f, Hz), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR, dB)
predicted_effect: 40-60% reduction in unexpected downtime by detecting mechanical faults 2-4 weeks before failure.
equations: THD = √(∑I_h²)/I_f × 100%, where THD is total harmonic distortion
SNR = 20log₁₀(I_fault/I_noise)
boundary_conditions: Effective for motors with load variations >20%; limited effectiveness in highly variable load environments or with power electronics filtering
cross_domain_transition: Wind power generation -> manufacturing, transferring electrical signature analysis from wind turbines to general industrial machinery monitoring

problem: Aerospace structures experience unpredictable fatigue loads due to varying operational conditions.
unexploited_phenomenon: Drivetrain dynamic analysis for optimizing loads in wind turbines as documented in the evidence.
intervention: Implement dynamic load optimization controllers in aerospace structures using real-time load monitoring and control surface adjustments.
governing_variables: Load distribution (L, N), stress concentration factor (K_t), fatigue cycles to failure (N_f)
predicted_effect: 25-40% reduction in structural fatigue damage in aerospace components through load redistribution.
equations: σ_max = K_t × σ_nominal
N_f = A(σ_max)^(-b) (Basquin's equation)
boundary_conditions: Effective for structures with controllable load paths; limited effectiveness for highly random or impulse loads
cross_domain_transition: Wind power generation -> aerospace, transferring load optimization techniques from wind turbines to aerospace structures

problem: High-power inverters for motor drives suffer from reliability failures due to excessive switching losses and thermal stress.
unexploited_phenomenon: Discontinuous pulse width modulation (DPWM) reduces switching losses by clamping phase voltage to DC bus during certain switching intervals.
intervention: Implement discontinuous PWM in flux angle control for induction motor drives to reduce switching losses under light load conditions.
governing_variables: Switching frequency (fsw, Hz), DC bus voltage (Vdc, V), load current (Iload, A), switching energy per cycle (Esw, J)
predicted_effect: 20-40% reduction in switching losses under light load conditions (0.3-0.6 pu) due to reduced number of switching transitions per fundamental cycle.
equations: Psw = fsw × Esw
Esw = (1/2) × Vdc × Iload × tsw
boundary_conditions: Effective at light to medium loads (0.3-0.6 pu), less effective at full load where continuous PWM may be preferable. Requires precise timing control.
cross_domain_transition: Motor drives to automotive electric vehicle powertrains, where reduced losses directly extend battery range and improve thermal management.

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Continuous PWM with fixed switching frequency, which maintains consistent switching losses regardless of load.
baseline.baseline_metric: Typical efficiency of 85-90% at light loads with conventional PWM.
baseline.candidate_metric: Predicted efficiency of 92-95% at light loads with DPWM implementation.
baseline.expected_delta: 5-10% absolute efficiency improvement at light loads.

killer_experiment.experiment: BENCH-scale test setup with induction motor drive, DPWM controller implementation, and efficiency/power analyzer comparing DPWM vs continuous PWM at various loads.
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether the efficiency improvement from reduced switching losses outweighs any potential increase in harmonic losses.
killer_experiment.kill_condition: If DPWM shows no improvement or degradation in total system efficiency compared to continuous PWM.

failure_modes.mitigation: mitigation through optimized switching pattern design

commercial_path.integration_point: Inverter control software/firmware in electric vehicle powertrain systems

problem: Data-center power supply units suffer from reliability failures due to thermal management challenges in high-power density applications.
unexploited_phenomenon: Wide-bandgap GaN devices offer superior thermal conductivity and switching characteristics compared to traditional silicon devices.
intervention: Replace traditional silicon-based converters with GaN-based modular multilevel converters for high-power density applications.
governing_variables: Thermal conductivity (k, W/m·K), operating temperature (T, °C), power density (W/cm³), switching frequency (fsw, Hz)
predicted_effect: 30-50% reduction in operating temperature due to superior thermal properties of GaN, leading to 2-3× longer component lifetime.
equations: Rth = Tj - Ta / P
Lth = k × A / d
boundary_conditions: Effective at high switching frequencies (>100 kHz), requires proper thermal management design. Most beneficial in high-power density applications (>1 kW/cm³).
cross_domain_transition: High-power motor drives to data-center power supplies, where improved thermal management directly improves reliability and reduces cooling requirements.

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Silicon-based IGBT converters with conventional thermal management.
baseline.baseline_metric: Typical junction temperature of 125-150°C with limited power density.
baseline.candidate_metric: Predicted junction temperature of 80-100°C with higher power density capability.

killer_experiment.experiment: LAB-scale thermal testing of GaN-based modules vs silicon-based modules under identical power loading conditions.
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether GaN devices maintain reliability advantages under long-term high-temperature cycling conditions.
killer_experiment.kill_condition: If GaN devices show no thermal advantage or exhibit unexpected failure modes under accelerated aging tests.

failure_modes.failure_mode: GaN device degradation under high voltage stress

technology_name: Phase-Shift DPWM for Thermally Limited Applications
problem: High-power inverters for motor drives suffer from reliability failures in thermally limited applications where heat dissipation is challenging.
unexploited_phenomenon: Phase-shift-based discontinuous PWM reduces switching losses by clamping phase voltage to DC bus while maintaining output quality.
intervention: Implement phase-shift-based DPWM in thermally limited high-power inverter applications to reduce switching losses and enable higher power density.
governing_variables: Switching frequency (fsw, Hz), phase shift angle (θ, degrees), DC bus voltage (Vdc, V), load current (Iload, A), thermal resistance (Rth, °C/W)
predicted_effect: 20-35% reduction in switching losses, enabling 15-25% increase in power density within the same thermal constraints.

boundary_conditions: Most effective in thermally limited applications where heat dissipation is the primary constraint. Requires precise phase shift control.
cross_domain_transition: Low-voltage micro inverters to aerospace high-power motor drives, where thermal management is critical for reliability in confined spaces.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: High-power inverter for motor drives experiences thermal limitations that constrain power density.
causal_chain: phase voltage clamped to DC bus
unexploited_phenomenon: Discontinuous PWM reduces switching losses by clamping phase voltage to DC bus (RECORD_ID: doi:10.3390/mi16101128)
intervention: Implement discontinuous PWM technique in flux angle control for induction motor drives
governing_variables: Switching frequency (fsw, Hz), DC bus voltage (Vdc, V), load current (I, A), thermal resistance (Rth, °C/W)
predicted_effect: 15-30% reduction in switching losses under light load conditions (RECORD_ID: doi:10.48308/ijrtei.2025.240319.1092)
equations: Psw = 0.5 * Vdc * I * fsw * tsw (switching losses), Ptotal = Psw + Pconduction (total losses)
boundary_conditions: Effective under light to medium load conditions; less beneficial at full load where conduction losses dominate
cross_domain_transition: power_electronics -> automotive (improves EV power density and range)

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Continuous PWM technique with higher switching frequency

killer_experiment.kill_condition: DPWM causes >15% increase in torque ripple or THD compared to continuous PWM

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

verified_bindings.span: In transportation electrification, power modules are considered the best choice for power switches to build a high-power inverter. Recently, several studies have presented prototypes that use parallel discrete MOSFETs and show similar overall output capabilities. This paper aims to compare the maximum output power and losses of inverters with different types

Both high-precision and high-efficient torque control of induction motor drives is an important research field due to the extensive use of these motors in torque-controlled applications, e.g. electric vehicles.

Abstract This paper revisits loss model control (LMC) of the 3‐phase induction motor (IM) and presents a robust LMC algorithm for medium‐sized pump drives. Compared with other power loss reduction algorithms for IM, the presented one has the advantages of fast and smooth flux adaptation, high accuracy, and versatile implementation.

The integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays for induction motor drives (IMDs) has attained a lot of research interest due to the versatile applications of IMD including water pumping, cement industries, electric vehicles, and rolling mills etc. Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are a prominent solution for driving medium voltage induction motors (IMs) due to their superior performances over two-level voltage source inverters (VSIs).

rejected_bindings.proposed_span: Three different motor drives for electric traction are compared, in terms of output power and efficiency at the same stack dimensions and inverter size. Induction motor (IM), surface-mounted permanent-magnet (PM) (SPM), and interior PM (IPM) synchronous motor drives are investigated, with reference to a common vehicle specification.

problem: High-precision torque control in electric vehicle motor drives is compromised by inverter nonlinearities and sensorless operation limitations.
causal_chain: gray-box observer combines first principles with data-driven modeling
unexploited_phenomenon: Gray-box models (GBMs) combine first-order principles from physics with data-driven modeling to achieve high-precision rotor flux estimation
intervention: Implementation of gray-box rotor flux observer and inverter model for induction motor drives
governing_variables: Flux estimation error (Δψ, Wb), torque ripple (ΔT, Nm), rotor time constant (τ_r, s), stator resistance (R_s, Ω)
predicted_effect: 40-60% reduction in flux estimation error compared to pure model-based approaches because GBMs adapt to system variations
equations: ψ_est = ψ_model + K * (ψ_measured - ψ_model), where K is adaptation gain
boundary_conditions: Effective in low to medium speed ranges; performance degrades at very low speeds where back-EMF is small
cross_domain_transition: power_electronics -> automotive + transferring high-precision flux control from industrial drives to electric vehicles improves torque response and efficiency

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Standard model-based flux observers with documented limitations at low speeds and under parameter variations
baseline.baseline_metric: 15-25% flux estimation error under varying load conditions
baseline.candidate_metric: 5-10% flux estimation error under same conditions
baseline.expected_delta: 10-15% absolute improvement in flux estimation accuracy

killer_experiment.experiment: Bench test with EV motor drive system, flux observer implementation, and torque measurement equipment
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether the improvement persists across different operating temperatures and aging conditions
killer_experiment.kill_condition: <10% improvement in flux estimation error compared to baseline

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

verified_bindings.span: Abstract This paper revisits loss model control (LMC) of the 3‐phase induction motor (IM) and presents a robust LMC algorithm for medium‐sized pump drives. Compared with other power loss reduction algorithms for IM, the presented one has the advantages of fast and smooth flux adaptation, high accuracy, and versatile implementation.

Three different motor drives for electric traction are compared, in terms of output power and efficiency at the same stack dimensions and inverter size. Induction motor (IM), surface-mounted permanent-magnet (PM) (SPM), and interior PM (IPM) synchronous motor drives are investigated, with reference to a common vehicle specification.
Compared with other power loss reduction algorithms for IM, the presented one has the advantages of fast and smooth flux adaptation, high accuracy, and versatile implementation.
An improved loss‐model for IM drive has been developed. The model considers the surplus power loss caused by inverter voltage harmonics and magnetic saturation using closed‐form equations.

verified_bindings.span: including thermal, electrical and energy management challenges, based on discussions at the 2nd Workshop on Thermal Management in Telecommunication Systems and Data Centers in Santa Clara, California, on April 25–26, 2012. The relevance of thermal management in electronic systems is reviewed against the background of the energy usage of the information technology (IT) industry, encompassing perspectives of different sectors of the industry.

A data centre can be defined as an infrastructure facility that houses file servers, processors and other computer equipment, along with a standby power supply. These servers are kept inside cabinets and those cabinets are called racks. These racks are located close to each other inside a data centre to form rows. These rows are located front to front and back to back to form the aisles.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

problem: Air-cooled heat exchangers have blind spots where condensation and fouling cannot be detected, leading to reduced efficiency and increased energy consumption.
unexploited_phenomenon: The relationship between surface temperature and condensation in heat exchangers can be modeled to predict fouling before it impacts performance.
intervention: Non-invasive temperature monitoring system with condensation/fouling prediction algorithm for air-cooled heat exchangers.
governing_variables: Surface temperature (T), relative humidity (RH), heat transfer coefficient (h), fouling factor (Rf)
predicted_effect: 15-25% reduction in energy consumption by detecting and addressing condensation and fouling 30-60 days earlier.
equations: Q = hA(T_surface - T_ambient), Rf = f(T, RH, time)
boundary_conditions: Valid for stable operating conditions; fails during rapid humidity changes or when heat exchanger geometry is unknown.
cross_domain_transition: Chemical process monitoring -> data center heat exchanger maintenance + transfer enables predictive maintenance of cooling systems

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Scheduled maintenance with no early detection of condensation/fouling
baseline.baseline_metric: 3-6 month maintenance intervals with 10-15% energy degradation between intervals
baseline.candidate_metric: 1-2 month maintenance intervals with 3-5% energy degradation between intervals
baseline.expected_delta: 50% reduction in energy degradation with 60% improvement in maintenance timing

killer_experiment.experiment: BENCH test with instrumented heat exchanger, comparing predictions against actual fouling measurements
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether temperature measurements can predict fouling with <5% error 30 days in advance
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Prediction error >10% in fouling factor estimation

commercial_path.integration_point: Maintenance scheduling system with early warning alerts
