problem: Data center aisles have thermal blind spots between racks where temperature gradients cannot be measured, leading to suboptimal cooling distribution.
unexploited_phenomenon: Thermal gradients between racks can be interpolated from perimeter measurements using spatial correlation models.
intervention: Perimeter sensor array with aisle-level thermal interpolation for hot/cold aisle containment.
governing_variables: Sensor spacing (d), thermal gradient magnitude (G), interpolation error (ε), airflow velocity (v)
predicted_effect: 20-35% improvement in cooling distribution by eliminating blind spots between racks with minimal additional sensors.
equations: ε = f(d, G, v), T_aisle(x,y) = T_rack + ∇T·r + ε
boundary_conditions: Valid for steady airflow conditions; fails during rapid equipment changes or when airflow patterns are chaotic.
cross_domain_transition: Remote sensing interpolation -> data center aisle thermal mapping + transfer enables efficient cooling with minimal sensors

baseline.baseline_incumbent: No inter-rack temperature measurements with uniform cooling distribution
baseline.baseline_metric: ±4°C temperature variation between racks
baseline.candidate_metric: ±2°C temperature variation between racks
baseline.expected_delta: 50% reduction in temperature variation between racks

killer_experiment.experiment: BENCH test with small-scale aisle mockup, comparing interpolated temperatures against actual measurements
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether perimeter measurements can predict aisle temperatures with <2°C error
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Interpolation error >2.5°C in any region

problem: Inefficient thermal prediction in air-cooled data centers leading to suboptimal cooling energy consumption
unexploited_phenomenon: Data-driven proper orthogonal decomposition for reduced order modeling of air-cooled systems
intervention: Implementation of a reduced order model using proper orthogonal decomposition on sensor data from air-cooled data centers
governing_variables: Number of spatial dimensions (n), Number of temporal modes (k), Sensor measurement accuracy (σ)
predicted_effect: 40-70% reduction in computational time for thermal prediction with <5% error in temperature prediction compared to full-order models
equations: X_k = U_k * S_k * V_k^T, where X_k is the reduced matrix, U_k and V_k are truncated singular vectors, S_k is the diagonal matrix of singular values
boundary_conditions: Valid for steady-state and quasi-steady thermal conditions; fails during rapid transient events not captured in training data

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Traditional full-order computational fluid dynamics modeling
baseline.baseline_metric: High computational cost (hours to days for single simulation)
baseline.candidate_metric: Minutes to hours for simulation with comparable accuracy

killer_experiment.experiment: Bench-scale test with computational time comparison between full-order and reduced-order models using identical thermal boundary conditions
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether the reduced-order model can maintain accuracy across varying operating conditions
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Error in temperature prediction exceeds 10% of actual measurements

failure_modes.mitigation: mitigation through periodic model retraining with new sensor data

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

verified_bindings.span: including thermal, electrical and energy management challenges, based on discussions at the 2nd Workshop on Thermal Management in Telecommunication Systems and Data Centers in Santa Clara, California, on April 25–26, 2012. The relevance of thermal management in electronic systems is reviewed against the background of the energy usage of the information technology (IT) industry, encompassing perspectives of different sectors of the industry.

A data centre can be defined as an infrastructure facility that houses file servers, processors and other computer equipment, along with a standby power supply. These servers are kept inside cabinets and those cabinets are called racks. These racks are located close to each other inside a data centre to form rows. These rows are located front to front and back to back to form the aisles.
Reduced order modeling of air-cooled data center using data-driven proper orthogonal decomposition

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

technology_name: Solar Adsorption Cooling with Evacuated Tube Collectors
problem: Commercial buildings in hot climates lose thermal energy through inefficient cooling systems that rely heavily on electricity.
unexploited_phenomenon: Solar adsorption cooling systems using evacuated tube collectors can provide cooling without electricity consumption in hot arid climates
intervention: Implementation of solar adsorption cooling systems using Evacuated Tube Collectors (ETCs) for commercial building cooling
governing_variables: Solar irradiance (W/m²), collector area (m²), COP of adsorption system, ambient temperature (°C)
predicted_effect: 40-70% reduction in electricity consumption for cooling because solar energy drives the refrigeration cycle
equations: Q_cooling = COP × Q_solar
COP_adsorption = Q_cooling / Q_input
η_collector = Q_collected / (A × I)
boundary_conditions: Most effective in hot, dry climates with high solar irradiance; performance decreases at night
cross_domain_transition: Solar thermal technology -> building cooling + direct heat utilization eliminates conversion losses

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Conventional vapor compression air conditioning systems
baseline.baseline_metric: Typical COP of 3-4 for electric air conditioning systems
baseline.candidate_metric: COP of 0.4-0.6 for solar adsorption systems but with 40-70% reduced electricity consumption
baseline.expected_delta: 40-70% reduction in electricity consumption for cooling

killer_experiment.experiment: Small-scale demonstration system with ETC collectors connected to adsorption chiller
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Real-world performance under varying solar conditions and building loads
killer_experiment.kill_condition: If solar contribution is less than 30% of total cooling energy requirement

commercial_path.buyer: Commercial building owners in hot climates
commercial_path.use_case: Cooling for commercial buildings in hot, dry regions
commercial_path.integration_point: Parallel integration with existing HVAC systems to supplement cooling capacity

technology_name: Deep Learning Predictive Model for Absorption Chiller Control
problem: Absorption chiller plants operate inefficiently due to inability to predict and respond to changing load conditions accurately.
unexploited_phenomenon: Deep learning predictive models can forecast cooling demand with greater accuracy than traditional methods, enabling proactive control adjustments
intervention: Implementation of deep learning predictive model for global optimization control of absorption chiller plants
governing_variables: Historical load data (kW), weather conditions (°C), humidity (%), chiller efficiency (COP), heat source temperature (°C)
predicted_effect: 20-30% improvement in thermal efficiency because predictive control enables optimal operation before demand changes
equations: Load_prediction = f(historical_load, weather, time)
COP = Q_cooling / Q_heat
Efficiency = actual_output / theoretical_max
boundary_conditions: Requires large datasets for training; performance depends on data quality and system complexity
cross_domain_transition: Predictive AI models -> thermal system control + anticipatory operation enables proactive efficiency improvements

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Traditional control strategies with reactive adjustments to current conditions
baseline.baseline_metric: Typical thermal efficiency of 60-70% for absorption chiller plants
baseline.candidate_metric: Predicted thermal efficiency of 75-85% with deep learning optimization

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. verified_bindings.span: Shell-and-tube heat exchangers often operate under harsh conditions that induce fouling, leading to loss of thermal efficiency, production downtime, and increased maintenance costs.

Heat exchanger failures in service—particularly tube-wall thinning, crack initiation, and eventual leakage—often originate from coupled damage mechanisms: corrosion/erosion, cyclic thermal stresses, and microstructural degradation that promotes void growth and coalescence.

verified_bindings.span: Heat exchanger failures in service—particularly tube-wall thinning, crack initiation, and eventual leakage—often originate from coupled damage mechanisms: corrosion/erosion, cyclic thermal stresses, and microstructural degradation that promotes void growth and coalescence.
Shell-and-tube heat exchangers often operate under harsh conditions that induce fouling, leading to loss of thermal efficiency, production downtime, and increased maintenance costs.

This article connects fundamental material-science concepts of void evolution and ductile fracture with practical reliability problems in shell-and-tube heat exchangers. By integrating void-growth/coalescence frameworks with remaining useful life (RUL) concepts for tube-wall loss and plugging criteria, we propose a fracture-aware pathway for diagnosing likely failure modes and improving predictive maintenance decisions.

The present work attempts to design and analyze experimentally hot water temperature difference, Nusselt number, Dean number, exergy loss, effectiveness and pressure drop in a shell, and triple meshed helical coil tube (TMHCT) heat exchanger.
Using baffles in exhaust mufflers is known to improve their transmission loss. The baffle cut ratio should affect the muffler performance analogous to a shell-and-tube heat exchanger.

The optimization of a shell and tube heat exchanger varies with the achieved heat transfer rate with a negligible amount of power consumption. The heat transfer rate becomes higher at a certain limit of baffle space and baffle number. However, in consequence, the pressure loss also increases with the increase of heat transfer rate.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

intervention: Integration of ultrasonic transducers into heat exchanger design for active fouling prevention
governing_variables: Ultrasonic frequency (kHz), power density (W/cm²), exposure time (s), fouling layer thickness (mm)
predicted_effect: 70-90% reduction in fouling rate, extending maintenance intervals by 3-5x

Fouling removal rate = k·I·t where k is removal coefficient, I is intensity, t is time
boundary_conditions: Effective for particulate and crystalline fouling; limited by soft, organic fouling that may re-adhere quickly
cross_domain_transition: Heat exchangers → Water treatment systems (ultrasonic anti-fouling in membrane systems)

verified_bindings.span: Shell-and-tube heat exchangers often operate under harsh conditions that induce fouling, leading to loss of thermal efficiency, production downtime, and increased maintenance costs.

Heat exchanger failures in service—particularly tube-wall thinning, crack initiation, and eventual leakage—often originate from coupled damage mechanisms: corrosion/erosion, cyclic thermal stresses, and microstructural degradation that promotes void growth and coalescence.

In this context, ultrasonic cavitation has been investigated as a strategy for fouling prevention and equipment cleaning, with the potential to reduce cleaning downtime or support in-service mitigation strategies.

unexploited_phenomenon: Branch baffle heat exchanger with mixed flow of oblique flow and local jet (RECORD_ID: title:64c86ebab0d0b9cf)
intervention: Replacement of traditional segmental baffles with branch baffles to optimize shell-side flow patterns

equations: Nu = f(Re, Pr, jet_velocity) where Nu is Nusselt number, Re is Reynolds number, Pr is Prandtl number
ΔP = μ·v·L/K where ΔP is pressure drop, μ is viscosity, v is velocity, L is length, K is permeability
boundary_conditions: Effective for shell-side flows with Reynolds numbers >3000; limited by very viscous fluids where jet formation is difficult

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Inaccurate temperature and heat mapping in conventional heat exchanger analysis methods
unexploited_phenomenon: Discrete thermal analysis methods for improved temperature and heat mapping (RECORD_ID: doi:10.1038/s41598-026-35215-z)
intervention: Implementation of discrete thermal analysis software for heat exchanger design and optimization
governing_variables: Discretization resolution (nodes/m), temperature accuracy (K), heat flux (W/m²), two-phase flow characteristics
predicted_effect: 15-25% improvement in design accuracy for complex heat exchanger configurations
equations: T_discrete = T_continuous + ε where T_discrete is discrete temperature, T_continuous is continuous temperature, ε is error term
Q = Σ(m·cp·ΔT) where Q is heat transfer, m is mass flow, cp is specific heat, ΔT is temperature difference
boundary_conditions: Effective for complex geometries and two-phase flows; limited by simple configurations where continuous methods are sufficient
cross_domain_transition: Heat exchangers -> Building HVAC systems (optimized thermal performance modeling)

problem: Suboptimal impeller geometry leading to high stress concentrations and accelerated material fatigue
unexploited_phenomenon: Inverse-design and optimization methods for centrifugal pump impellers (RECORD_ID: doi:10.3990/1.9789036527026)
intervention: Impeller designed using inverse optimization algorithms to minimize stress concentrations
governing_variables: Stress concentration factor Kt, blade loading coefficient CL, impeller outlet width b (m)
predicted_effect: 40-60% reduction in stress concentration factors
equations: Stress σ = Kt·σ_nominal, where σ_nominal is nominal stress without concentration
boundary_conditions: Effective for impeller diameters 0.1-1.0m; fails with extremely high rotational speeds (>5000 rpm)
cross_domain_transition: aerospace turbine blade optimization -> industrial pump impeller design

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Standard impeller designs based on empirical correlations (RECORD_ID: doi:10.1007/0-387-23263-x_9)
baseline.baseline_metric: Standard impellers show stress concentration factors of 2.0-3.0 in critical regions
baseline.candidate_metric: Stress concentration factors reduced to 1.2-1.8 in all regions

killer_experiment.experiment: Computational simulation with finite element analysis of stress distribution in optimized vs standard impellers, followed by physical strain gauge testing on prototype impellers
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether computational optimization translates to real-world stress reduction
killer_experiment.kill_condition: If optimized impellers show >10% higher stress concentrations than predicted by simulations

FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Cavitation-induced performance degradation in centrifugal pumps under varying operating conditions.
unexploited_phenomenon: Independent rotation of inducer and centrifugal impeller (RECORD_ID: doi:10.70675/67ab9b20za68fz4a17zb810z6b86831dcd6e)
intervention: A variable geometry inducer with adjustable blade angles that can be modified based on operating conditions to maintain optimal flow characteristics.
governing_variables: Blade angle adjustment (θ, degrees), rotational speed (ω, rpm), fluid viscosity (μ, Pa·s), inlet pressure (P_in, Pa)
predicted_effect: 20-40% reduction in cavitation-induced efficiency loss because cavitation inception scales with local pressure distribution which can be optimized by geometry adjustment
equations: σ = (P_in - P_v) / (0.5 * ρ * v²) where σ is cavitation number, P_v is vapor pressure, ρ is fluid density, v is flow velocity
θ = f(Q, ω) where blade angle is function of flow rate and speed
boundary_conditions: Effective for Reynolds numbers > 10,000; limited by mechanical complexity at very high rotational speeds (>10,000 rpm)
cross_domain_transition: industrial_pumps -> energy (variable geometry control from pumps to wind turbine blade pitch control for varying wind conditions)

problem: Erosion damage from solid particles suspended in process fluids.
unexploited_phenomenon: Manufacturing improvements to surface treatments (RECORD_ID: doi:10.17918/00007954)
intervention: Micro-scale surface texturing inspired by marine organism shells that resist erosion through controlled energy dissipation.
governing_variables: Surface feature height (h, μm), feature spacing (s, μm), particle impact angle (α, degrees), particle velocity (v, m/s)
predicted_effect: 30-50% reduction in material erosion rate because the textured surface redirects impact energy through controlled deformation rather than material removal
equations: Erosion rate = k * (v^n) / (h^m) where k is material constant, n and m are exponents dependent on material properties
Feature spacing s = λ * d_p where λ is spacing factor and d_p is particle diameter
boundary_conditions: Effective for particle sizes 10-500 μm; limited by feature manufacturing precision at sub-10 μm scales
cross_domain_transition: industrial_pumps -> marine (erosion-resistant surfaces from pump components to ship hulls for reduced biofouling and sediment adhesion)

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Standard hardened steel or ceramic coatings
baseline.baseline_metric: 0.1-0.5 mm/year material loss in abrasive conditions (RECORD_ID: doi:10.1007/0-387-23263-x_10)
baseline.candidate_metric: 0.05-0.25 mm/year material loss

killer_experiment.experiment: Accelerated erosion test chamber with controlled particle flow, sample coupons with different surface textures, precision weighing before and after testing, microscopy analysis of surface damage
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether the micro-texturing maintains its effectiveness under long-term cyclic loading
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Surface analysis shows no significant difference in erosion patterns between textured and control samples

failure_modes.mitigation: optimized feature geometry for energy dissipation

failure_modes.failure_mode: Clogging of features with fine particles
failure_modes.mitigation: self-cleaning feature design with directional flow

commercial_path.integration_point: External surfaces exposed to abrasive marine environments

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. problem: Fractured formations during drilling operations cause significant fluid loss and operational delays.
unexploited_phenomenon: Temperature-activated nanomaterial-enhanced liquid-solid phase transition emulsion that adapts to varying fracture apertures
intervention: Injection of temperature-activated nanomaterial-enhanced phase transition emulsion into fractured formations
governing_variables: Temperature (°C), fracture aperture (mm), nanomaterial concentration (wt%), oil-to-water ratio
predicted_effect: 70-90% reduction in fluid loss because the plugging efficiency scales with crosslinking density and nanomaterial surface area
equations: Plugging efficiency (%) = k × [nanomaterial] × T × (1/ΔP), where k is a constant, [nanomaterial] is concentration (wt%), T is temperature (°C), ΔP is pressure differential (MPa)
boundary_conditions: Effective at temperatures >80°C and fracture apertures <5mm; ineffective in high-salinity formations
cross_domain_transition: Water infrastructure drilling technology -> Oil & gas well drilling (transfer creates value by reducing drilling fluid loss in high-temperature formations)

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Conventional plugging materials (calcium carbonate, walnut shells) with documented poor compatibility with varying fracture apertures

killer_experiment.experiment: Laboratory-scale fracture simulation apparatus with temperature control, treating fractured core samples with emulsion vs. conventional plugging materials, measuring fluid loss rate
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: The temperature threshold for effective phase transition
killer_experiment.kill_condition: If plugging efficiency is <60% at target temperatures

A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Expensive control of distillation columns due to complex dynamics and computational requirements of high-fidelity models

intervention: Implement dynamic discrepancy reduced-order modeling framework for distillation column control
governing_variables: Model order reduction factor (r, dimensionless), computational time reduction ratio (τ, dimensionless), model accuracy (ε, %)

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Stroke Round 58; applies to all latent-variable inventions)
warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

intervention: Implement admicellar polymerization with optimized surfactant concentration in continuous stirred-tank reactors
governing_variables: Surfactant concentration (C, mol/L), interfacial area (A, m²), monomer conversion (%), reaction rate (r, mol/L·s)
predicted_effect: 30-50% reduction in waste stream generation due to improved selectivity and reduced byproducts
equations: Conversion = ∫r dt
Interfacial area = f(C, A_monomer)
boundary_conditions: Effective for polymerization reactions with moderate molecular weight; fails for high molecular weight polymers with complex architectures
cross_domain_transition: chemical_process -> chemical_process (same domain with improved reaction conditions)

problem: Inefficient Fischer-Tropsch synthesis due to suboptimal reactor design leading to poor catalytic performance.
unexploited_phenomenon: Microchannel reactors exhibit pronounced process intensification compared with conventional fixed-bed reactors through optimized geometric variables.
intervention: Multi-objective optimization of microchannel reactor geometry using CFD coupled with gradient-enhanced neural networks to systematically evaluate geometric variables.
governing_variables: Characteristic geometric variables (channel diameter, length, spacing, shape), catalyst loading, fluid velocity, temperature
predicted_effect: 30-50% increase in catalytic performance due to optimized flow distribution and heat transfer characteristics
equations: η = f(χ₁, χ₂, χ₃, χ₄) where η is catalytic performance and χ₁-χ₄ are characteristic geometric variables
∂η/∂χᵢ > 0 for optimized parameters
boundary_conditions: Holds for multi-tubular microchannel reactors with consistent catalyst loading; fails at extreme aspect ratios or when pressure drop constraints are violated
cross_domain_transition: chemical processing -> energy: Transfer microchannel optimization from chemical synthesis to energy production where catalytic performance directly impacts fuel efficiency

baseline.baseline_metric: Standard catalytic yield (g product/g catalyst/hour) with uncertainty ±5%

problem: Plant-model mismatches in advanced process control leading to suboptimal performance and increased operational costs.
unexploited_phenomenon: Dynamic discrepancy reduced-order modeling that balances computational complexity and model accuracy by combining first-principles components with black-box functions.
intervention: Implementation of gray-box models combining first-principles components with black-box functions to represent critical process dynamics
governing_variables: Model accuracy, computational complexity, plant-model mismatch, control horizon
predicted_effect: 25-40% reduction in control error and 20-30% decrease in computational requirements compared to full first-principles models
equations: Error = f(|P - M|) where P is plant behavior and M is model prediction
Complexity = g(Principles, BlackBox) where Principles is first-principles component complexity and BlackBox is black-box component complexity
boundary_conditions: Holds for processes with moderate nonlinearity and identifiable dominant dynamics; fails for highly chaotic or poorly understood processes
cross_domain_transition: chemical processing -> industrial manufacturing: Transfer gray-box modeling from chemical processes to general industrial control systems

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Full first-principles models with high computational requirements or purely empirical models with limited extrapolation
baseline.baseline_metric: Control error (±5-10%), computational time (minutes per control cycle)
baseline.candidate_metric: Control error (±2-5%), computational time (seconds per control cycle)
baseline.expected_delta: 50-80% reduction in control error, 70-90% reduction in computational time

killer_experiment.experiment: Bench-scale process simulation with real-time control implementation
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether the gray-box approach maintains accuracy across different operating conditions
killer_experiment.kill_condition: >3x increase in computational time or >2x increase in control error compared to baseline

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

technology_name: Dual Linear Kalman Filter Virtual Metrology
problem: Inability to measure and track gradual variations in the Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) process in real-time, leading to process drift and defects.
unexploited_phenomenon: Dynamic tracking of gradual data variations using Dual Linear Kalman Filter (DLKF) to jointly update state and parameters in real-time
intervention: Implementation of DLKF-based virtual metrology system for CMP process monitoring
governing_variables: Material Removal Rate (MRR), state variables, parameter estimates, measurement noise covariance, process noise covariance (units: nm/min, dimensionless)
predicted_effect: 30-60% reduction in process variation tracking error because DLKF dynamically adapts to process changes
equations: x_k = F_k * x_{k-1} + B_k * u_k + w_k
z_k = H_k * x_k + v_k
where x is state, F is state transition matrix, B is control input matrix, u is control input, w is process noise, z is measurement, H is observation matrix, v is measurement noise
boundary_conditions: Holds for processes with gradual variations; fails for sudden, discontinuous changes exceeding filter adaptation capability
cross_domain_transition: NONE (same domain)

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Traditional metrology methods with periodic measurements
baseline.baseline_metric: Periodic sampling with minutes-to-hours delay between measurements
baseline.candidate_metric: Real-time continuous monitoring with <1 second latency

killer_experiment.experiment: BENCH-scale testbed with CMP simulator implementing DLKF vs conventional sampling, comparing prediction accuracy against ground truth measurements
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether DLKF can accurately track gradual process variations in a simulated CMP environment
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Prediction error exceeds conventional method by >20%

commercial_path.integration_point: Between CMP tool metrology and process control systems

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.mechanism: OSV-4: HRV/autonomic state as orthogonal predictor for R2-C3
warnings.lesson: A signal can be GENUINELY ORTHOGONAL to a specific measurement architecture (Hakim measures pressure, not HRV) and still be a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of the same physiological variable (ICP → sympathetic → HRV). Orthogonality to one architecture does not imply independence from the underlying physiology. Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.
