problem: Inefficient thermal management in internal combustion engines leads to energy waste and reduced performance.
unexploited_phenomenon: Regeneration in internal combustion engines through thermal-hydraulic modeling and analysis of heat recovery systems.
intervention: Implementation of a regenerative thermal management system using thermal-hydraulic modeling to optimize heat recovery.
governing_variables: Heat recovery rate (kW), thermal storage capacity (kJ), temperature differential (°C), heat transfer efficiency (%)
predicted_effect: 10-20% improvement in engine efficiency through effective capture and reuse of otherwise wasted thermal energy.
equations: Heat recovery rate Q = h × A × ΔT, where h is heat transfer coefficient, A is surface area, and ΔT is temperature difference
Efficiency η = Q_recovered / Q_input × 100%
boundary_conditions: Effective for internal combustion engines with sufficient temperature differentials for heat recovery; effectiveness varies with engine load and operating conditions.
cross_domain_transition: Automotive thermal systems -> industrial energy recovery, applying engine thermal regeneration techniques to industrial waste heat recovery.

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Standard internal combustion engine cooling systems without heat recovery capabilities.
baseline.baseline_metric: Standard thermal efficiency of internal combustion engines (typically 25-35%).

killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: The actual efficiency improvement achievable across different engine operating conditions.
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Less than 5% improvement in thermal efficiency under any standard operating condition.

problem: Traditional internal combustion engines experience significant temperature cycles leading to thermal stress and reduced efficiency.
unexploited_phenomenon: Internal combustion engines with limited temperature cycles to reduce thermal stress and improve efficiency.
intervention: Design and implementation of internal combustion engines with controlled temperature cycles through advanced cooling systems.
governing_variables: Temperature fluctuation range (°C), thermal stress (MPa), component lifespan (hours), thermal efficiency (%)
predicted_effect: 15-25% improvement in component lifespan and 5-10% improvement in thermal efficiency through reduced thermal stress.
equations: Thermal stress σ = α × E × ΔT, where α is coefficient of thermal expansion, E is Young's modulus, and ΔT is temperature change

boundary_conditions: Effective for internal combustion engines where thermal stress is a limiting factor; may require significant redesign of cooling systems.
cross_domain_transition: Automotive engine design -> power generation, applying temperature cycle control techniques to improve power generation equipment reliability.

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Structural health monitoring systems reduce maintenance costs but their economic impact remains underexplored, particularly in cost-benefit terms.
unexploited_phenomenon: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) using microscopic techniques for composite materials
intervention: Embedded microscopic sensors in multi-material structures with AI-driven damage assessment
governing_variables: Detection sensitivity (μm), sensor density (m^-2), material degradation rate (%/cycle)
predicted_effect: 40-60% reduction in maintenance costs because early detection prevents catastrophic failures requiring full replacement
equations: C_maintenance = C_inspection * f + C_replacement * (1 - f), where f is failure probability reduced by SHM
boundary_conditions: Effective for composite and multi-material interfaces, limited by sensor resolution for sub-micron damage
cross_domain_transition: Aerospace composite monitoring -> industrial heavy equipment structural monitoring (creates value by extending asset lifespan in harsh operating environments)

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Scheduled maintenance with visual inspections and non-destructive testing
baseline.baseline_metric: 15-20% unplanned downtime, 25-30% of maintenance costs reactive
baseline.candidate_metric: 5-10% unplanned downtime, 10-15% of maintenance costs reactive
baseline.expected_delta: 50-70% reduction in unplanned downtime and 40-60% reduction in reactive maintenance costs

killer_experiment.experiment: Laboratory accelerated aging test of monitored vs non-monitored industrial components under cyclic loading, comparing failure detection timing and accuracy
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: False positive rate in complex multi-material environments
killer_experiment.kill_condition: False positive rate >20% or false negative rate >5%

failure_modes.mitigation: mitigation through surface treatment and mechanical interlocking
mitigation through shielding and signal processing algorithms

problem: Balancing weight reduction with structural stiffness in multi-material aircraft structures is challenging due to manufacturing tolerances.
causal_chain: Multi-material design strategy (CFRP spars, foam cores, aluminum joints)
unexploited_phenomenon: Tolerance-driven lightweight design and interface robustness of multi-material structures
intervention: Multi-material design with optimized interface geometry to accommodate manufacturing variations
governing_variables: Material stiffness (Pa), interface area (m²), tolerance variation (m)
predicted_effect: 20-30% weight reduction while maintaining structural integrity because interface geometry compensates for manufacturing variations
equations: σ = F/A, where A is optimized interface area accounting for tolerance variations
boundary_conditions: Effective for bonded multi-material interfaces, limited by extreme tolerance variations beyond statistical control
cross_domain_transition: Aerospace multi-material design -> automotive lightweight body structures (creates value by improving fuel efficiency without compromising safety)

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Uniform material sections with safety factor overdesign
baseline.baseline_metric: 25-30% of vehicle mass from structural components
baseline.candidate_metric: 15-20% of vehicle mass from structural components
baseline.expected_delta: 30-40% reduction in structural mass while maintaining or improving crash performance

killer_experiment.experiment: Finite element analysis of optimized multi-material joints under controlled tolerance variations, comparing stress distribution and failure modes
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Long-term durability under cyclic loading with interface stress concentrations
killer_experiment.kill_condition: Interface failure at tolerance variation < manufacturer's specification

failure_modes.mitigation: mitigation through surface treatment and optimized adhesive selection

warnings.mechanism: Stroke: clot-vessel adhesion isolation + measurement + strategy selection (Layer A: force-decomposition estimator v1)
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

problem: Progressive damage in composite structures is difficult to predict and validate, particularly after repairs.
unexploited_phenomenon: Progressive damage analysis technique using finite element method and test validation
intervention: Digital twin system with physics-based damage progression modeling
governing_variables: Failure strain threshold (%), damage propagation rate (mm/cycle), residual strength (Pa)

cross_domain_transition: Aerospace composite damage analysis -> civil infrastructure monitoring (creates value by extending infrastructure lifespan through predictive maintenance)

unexploited_phenomenon: Damage assessment on aircraft composite structure due to lightning constraints
intervention: Composite materials with embedded conductive networks for lightning protection
governing_variables: Electrical conductivity (S/m), lightning current density (A/m²), thermal expansion mismatch (K^-1)

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

problem: Industrial robot joints exhibit flexibility and kinematic errors that cause position errors and energy inefficiency during operation.
unexploited_phenomenon: Using robot joint flexibility as a double force sensor (RECORD_ID: title:eaad64fa212f97c4)
intervention: Implement variable structure control (VSC) that exploits joint flexibility to reduce energy loss
governing_variables: Joint stiffness (k, N/m), strain gauge sensitivity (S, µε/N), control sampling frequency (f, Hz)
predicted_effect: 20-40% reduction in energy consumption due to reduced corrective movements
equations: F = k·x (Hooke's law), ε = S·F (strain relationship)
boundary_conditions: Works best in low-precision, high-compliance tasks; fails in high-precision, rigid applications
cross_domain_transition: Climbing robot force sensing -> industrial robot joint control (exploits existing mechanical properties for sensing)

killer_experiment.kill_condition: If VSC system consumes more energy than traditional control (>10% increase)

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

problem: Industrial robots consume energy through redundant sensing and positioning systems.

intervention: Integrate polarimetric sensing to reduce reliance on multiple positioning sensors
governing_variables: Polarization sensitivity (S, dimensionless), measurement precision (σ, rad), angular resolution (θ, deg)

cross_domain_transition: Polarimetric sensing -> industrial robot positioning (applies optical sensing techniques to reduce energy consumption)

problem: Industrial robot arms have limited sensing capabilities in their operational blind spots, reducing their effectiveness in complex tasks.
unexploited_phenomenon: Imaging Stokes Polarimeter Using a Six-Axis Robot Arm (RECORD_ID: doi:10.1109/isot.2014.66)
intervention: Integration of a polarimetric sensing array at the robot's end effector
governing_variables: Stokes parameters (S0, S1, S2, S3), surface reflectance properties, incident angle
predicted_effect: 40-70% reduction in blind spot detection range because polarimetric sensitivity scales with surface material properties
equations: S = [S0, S1, S2, S3] where S0 = I_x + I_y, S1 = I_x - I_y, S2 = I_45 - I_135, S3 = I_rcp - I_lcp (intensities in different polarization states)
boundary_conditions: Works best on non-metallic surfaces; fails on perfectly reflective or completely absorbing surfaces
cross_domain_transition: Optical polarimetry -> industrial robotics + enables material-specific sensing in blind spots

warnings.lesson: A signal can be GENUINELY ORTHOGONAL to a specific measurement architecture (Hakim measures pressure, not HRV) and still be a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of the same physiological variable (ICP → sympathetic → HRV). Orthogonality to one architecture does not imply independence from the underlying physiology. Before claiming a signal is 'new information,' test whether it is causally downstream of an already-measured variable. If A → B and A is measured, then B is a proxy for A, not new information — even if B is measured by a different sensor.

warnings.mechanism: Stroke: clot-vessel adhesion isolation + measurement + strategy selection (Layer A: force-decomposition estimator v1)
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Stroke Round 58; applies to all latent-variable inventions)
warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

intervention: Integration of AR vision system with depth perception capabilities

predicted_effect: 50-80% reduction in collision incidents because depth accuracy scales with camera baseline distance

boundary_conditions: Effective in well-limited warehouse environments; struggles with highly reflective surfaces or extreme darkness
cross_domain_transition: AR visualization -> warehouse robotics + creates comprehensive environmental awareness

killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Performance degradation in varying lighting conditions typical of warehouses
killer_experiment.kill_condition: <30% improvement in collision avoidance rate

intervention: Implementation of joint error compensation algorithms

cross_domain_transition: Precision machining -> robotic gripping + enables high-precision manipulation in confined spaces

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Robotic grippers suffer from reliability failures due to inadequate force sensing in confined spaces where external sensors cannot be installed.

unexploited_phenomenon: Using the own flexibility of a climbing robot as a double force sensor (RECORD_ID: title:eaad64fa212f97c4)
intervention: Development of gripper links with optimized stiffness and integrated strain gauges for force sensing
governing_variables: Link stiffness (N/m), strain gauge sensitivity (µε/N), material Young's modulus (Pa)
predicted_effect: 70-90% reduction in object damage because force sensing allows adaptive gripping force control
equations: F = k·ε, where F is force (N), k is stiffness (N/m), ε is strain (m/m)
boundary_conditions: Effective for grippers with appropriate stiffness selection; limited by material fatigue after repeated cycles
cross_domain_transition: climbing robotics -> industrial grippers

baseline.baseline_incumbent: External force sensors or fixed-force grippers
baseline.baseline_metric: 30-50% damage rate for delicate objects (RECORD_ID: title:eaad64fa212f97c4)

killer_experiment.experiment: Bench test with gripper handling delicate objects of varying fragility; compare damage rates between conventional grippers and flexibility-based force sensing grippers

killer_experiment.kill_condition: Damage rate reduction less than 50% compared to conventional grippers

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

If the mechanics and electronics systems are contained inside the own robot, the robot becomes portable without external control. Commercial force sensors cannot be used due to limited space and weight.

By selecting the links material with appropriate stiffness and placing strain gauges on the structure, the own robot flexibility can be used such as force sensor. Thus, forces applied on the robot tip can be measured without additional external devices.
Commercial force sensors cannot be used due to limited space and weight.

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Center pivot irrigation systems waste water through non-uniform water distribution and evaporation losses.
unexploited_phenomenon: Dual-diameter laterals in center pivot irrigation systems can optimize water distribution by adjusting flow velocity along the lateral length.
intervention: Replace standard uniform-diameter laterals with dual-diameter laterals in center pivot irrigation systems.
governing_variables: Lateral diameter (m), flow velocity (m/s), pressure (kPa), nozzle spacing (m)
predicted_effect: 15-30% reduction in water waste due to improved distribution uniformity, as evidenced by RECORD_ID: doi:10.3390/w14152292
equations: DU = 100(1 - 0.025V), where DU is distribution uniformity (%), V is variance in application depth
Q = A×v, where Q is flow rate (m³/s), A is cross-sectional area (m²), v is velocity (m/s)
boundary_conditions: Effective in flat terrain with uniform soil types; less effective on slopes or with highly variable soil infiltration rates

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

problem: Traditional irrigation systems apply water uniformly regardless of actual crop needs, leading to water waste and potential runoff.
unexploited_phenomenon: IoT-based automated monitoring systems can enable precision irrigation by providing real-time data for optimized water application, as evidenced in RECORD_ID: doi:10.58694/20.500.12479/2947
intervention: Deploy IoT sensor networks with automated control systems for precision irrigation management.
governing_variables: Sensor density (sensors/ha), data transmission frequency (Hz), irrigation response time (min), water application accuracy (%)
predicted_effect: 20-40% reduction in water waste through precision application based on IoT monitoring capabilities
equations: W_s = θ_v × ρ_b × d × A, where W_s is soil water content (m³), θ_v is volumetric water content (%), ρ_b is bulk density (kg/m³), d is depth (m), A is area (m²)
Q = A × IR × t, where Q is water applied (m³), A is area (m²), IR is irrigation rate (mm/hr), t is time (hr)
boundary_conditions: Effective in diverse soil types and crop systems; less effective in areas with poor connectivity or power availability for IoT devices
cross_domain_transition: Electronics/telecom (IoT monitoring) -> agriculture (precision irrigation)

baseline.baseline_incumbent: Time-scheduled irrigation systems with documented limitation of inflexible water application regardless of actual needs
baseline.baseline_metric: Water application efficiency of 60-75% in conventional irrigation systems
baseline.candidate_metric: Water application efficiency of 80-90% with IoT-based precision irrigation

killer_experiment.experiment: BENCH-scale test with IoT sensors controlling a mini-irrigation system, comparing water application accuracy against time-scheduled control
killer_experiment.decisive_uncertainty: Whether IoT sensors can provide sufficiently accurate and timely data for precise irrigation control in field conditions
killer_experiment.kill_condition: If IoT system shows no improvement in water application accuracy or introduces unacceptable delays in response

problem: Traditional sprinkler packages in center pivot systems create water distribution inefficiencies leading to runoff and evaporation losses.
unexploited_phenomenon: Rotating plate or wobble-plate spray heads combine advantages of different sprinkler types to improve water distribution patterns as evidenced in RECORD_ID: title:816569c4bce9ccdf
intervention: Replace traditional sprinkler packages with optimized rotating plate sprinklers in center pivot systems.
governing_variables: Droplet size distribution (mm), application rate (mm/hr), throw radius (m), wind drift factor (-)
predicted_effect: 20-35% reduction in water waste through improved distribution uniformity based on sprinkler pattern analysis
equations: DU = 100(1 - 0.025V), where DU is distribution uniformity (%), V is variance in application depth
D = k × v^0.5, where D is droplet diameter (mm), k is sprinkler constant, v is velocity (m/s)
boundary_conditions: Effective in various wind conditions and field configurations; less effective in extreme wind conditions or on highly irregular terrain
cross_domain_transition: Fluid dynamics (sprinkler design) -> agriculture (irrigation efficiency)

A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson:

Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-016 (sharpened per CEO Round 58): A proposed latent quantity survives only when (1) identifiability is demonstrated under an EXPLICIT observation/dynamics model with full rank/observability analysis (not naive unknown-count), AND (2) identifiability REMAINS under plausible model uncertainty (each ideal assumption relaxed toward realistic physics and re-tested). A single favorable rank calculation under a convenient model is INSUFFICIENT. A single unfavorable perturbation model is ALSO INSUFFICIENT to claim universal non-identifiability — it only kills the specific estimator tested under that specific perturbation model. The correct procedure: (a) define state, observables, inputs, noise, known/unknown params; (b) build measurement equations; (c) test rank of Jacobian wrt unknown params; (d) perform adversarial model-uncertainty test: relax each assumption toward realistic physics and re-test identifiability under the combined relaxed model; (e) only if BOTH the ideal-model rank AND the adversarial-model rank hold (or constructively fail) can a universal claim (measurable OR non-measurable) be recorded.

warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.
warnings.action_required: Explicit justification required to proceed despite this constraint

problem: Undetected porosity in concrete leads to water infiltration, freeze-thaw damage, and premature structural degradation
unexploited_phenomenon: AI-driven semantic segmentation for concrete porosity prediction via CT imaging
intervention: ECS-Net neural network that analyzes CT scans to identify and quantify porosity in concrete structures
governing_variables: CT resolution (μm), grayscale contrast, pore morphology, network accuracy (%), detection threshold (mm³)
predicted_effect: 90-95% accuracy in detecting pores >0.1mm³, enabling early intervention before degradation occurs
equations: Porosity (%) = V_pores/V_total × 100
